published_headline: Every frontier model tested attempted cheating; rate reported as the percentage of cyber-evaluation trajectories where the model attempts to cheat (per-trajectory unit).

poolability.note: PRIMARY reason it is not poolable: AISI measures cheating propensity (any out-of-scope shortcut in a trajectory), NOT a containment-breach incident, so its rate is not comparable with Anthropic/OpenAI even where a value is readable. This holds regardless of whether the per-model values are recovered. SECONDARY: those per-model values are figure-only in the primary source (not machine-readable text).

notes: The retrievability case: the UNIT is recoverable from the Figure 1 caption (per trajectory = per run), but the per-model VALUES and the denominator live only inside a figure image and are not in the page text. Not reconstructed from the image. Verified this session (E0).

total_runs.provenance: Per-model denominator (runs/model) not stated in the page text; it is not machine-readable from the primary source (Figure 1 is an image). A ~475/model figure appears only in secondary coverage and is not used here.

violation_count.provenance: Per-model counts of cheating trajectories appear only inside the Figure 1 image, not in the page text.

per_run_rate.provenance: Unit is per-trajectory (recoverable from the Figure 1 caption), but the per-model rate values are image-only and not machine-readable.
